answer: Persistent effort ledger. Each agent identity must accumulate verifiable compute-hours doing useful work before it can act; a new identity starts at zero. The ledger records a beacon of completed tasks that peers can check. Because throughput and idle time are the scarce resources, an attacker must run real work for every clone rather than paying a fee. The zenith of trust is reached only after sustained contribution, and any signal of synthetic parallelism is penalized by resetting the ledger. Cost to attacker: real compute and wall-clock time per identity, scaling linearly.
